title: "plot for eda"
output: html_document

```{r load data, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#check data type and missing value
library(tidyverse)
data <- read.csv("low2076upd.csv")
#colSums(is.na(data))
#head(data)
```

```{r}
categorical_vars <- c("Y", "A", "SEX", "EDUCATION", 
                      paste0("PAY_", c(0, 2:6)))

data <- data %>% mutate(across(all_of(categorical_vars), as.factor))
```



```{r}
#Categorical (PAY_0 to PAY_6)
data %>%
  select(starts_with("PAY_") & !starts_with("PAY_AMT")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Month", values_to = "Status") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Status)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "orange") +
  facet_wrap(~ Month) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Payment Status Indicators over 6 Months",
       x = "Payment Status",
       y = "Count")

#Continuous (BILL_AMT1 to BILL_AMT6)
data %>%
  select(starts_with("BILL_AMT")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Month", values_to = "Amount") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Amount)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "red", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ Month, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distributions of Monthly Bill Amounts",
       x = "Bill Amount",
       y = "Frequency")

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/bill_amounts_distribution.png", width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

#Continuous (PAY_AMT1 to PAY_AMT6)
data %>%
  select(starts_with("PAY_AMT")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Month", values_to = "Amount") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Amount)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "green", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ Month, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distributions of Monthly Payment Amounts",
       x = "Payment Amount",
       y = "Frequency")

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/payment_amounts_distribution.png", width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```


```{r}
library(scales)
# 2&3.
# Continuous Covariates vs Treatment (A) and Outcome (Y) 
continuous_vars <- data %>%
  select(A, Y, AGE, LIMIT_BAL, starts_with("BILL"), starts_with("PAY_A"))

continuous_long <- continuous_vars %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(A, Y), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value")

#Do continuous variables predict Treatment Enrollment (L -> A)?
p_cont_A <- ggplot(continuous_long, aes(x = A, y = Value, fill = A)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Continuous Covariates by PPP Enrollment (A)",
       x = "PPP Enrollment (A)", y = "Value") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# log here just for better visualization
p_cont_A_log <- ggplot(continuous_long, aes(x = factor(A), y = Value, fill = factor(A))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = "pseudo_log",
    # 1. Reduce the number of labels
    n.breaks = 2, 
    # 2. Use short labels (K for thousands, M for millions)
    labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale()) 
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # 3. Shrink the font size slightly for better fit
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Continuous Covariates by Enrollment (A)",
       subtitle = "(Log-Scaled for better visualization)",
       x = "PPP Enrollment (A)", y = "Value (Log Scale)")

print(p_cont_A_log)

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/continuous_by_treatment_log.png", 
       plot = p_cont_A_log, 
       width = 12, 
       height = 10, 
       dpi = 300)

#Do continuous variables predict Default (L -> Y)?
p_cont_Y_log <- ggplot(continuous_long, aes(x = factor(Y), y = Value, fill = factor(Y))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = "pseudo_log",
    n.breaks = 2, 
    labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale()) 
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Continuous Covariates by Default Status (Y)",
       subtitle = "(Log-Scaled for better visualization)",
       x = "Default Status (Y)", y = "Value (Log Scale)")

print(p_cont_Y_log)

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/continuous_by_default_log.png", 
       plot = p_cont_Y_log, 
       width = 12, 
       height = 10, 
       dpi = 300)

```


```{r}
# Categorical Covariates vs Treatment (A) and Outcome (Y)

categorical_vars <- data %>%
  select(A, Y, SEX, EDUCATION, starts_with("PAY_") & !starts_with("PAY_AMT"))

categorical_long <- categorical_vars %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(A, Y), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Category") 

#Do categorical variables predict Treatment Enrollment (L -> A)?
p_cat_A <- ggplot(categorical_long, aes(x = Category, fill = A)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + # show proportions 
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of PPP Enrollment (A) across Categorical Covariates",
       x = "Covariate Category", y = "Proportion of Enrollment")

print(p_cat_A)

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/categorical_by_treatment_proportions.png", 
       plot = p_cat_A, 
       width = 14, 
       height = 10, 
       dpi = 300)

#Do categorical variables predict Default (L -> Y)?
p_cat_Y <- ggplot(categorical_long, aes(x = Category, fill = Y)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Default (Y) across Categorical Covariates",
       x = "Covariate Category", y = "Proportion Defaulting")

print(p_cat_Y)

ggsave("OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/categorical_by_default_proportions.png", 
       plot = p_cat_Y, 
       width = 14, 
       height = 10, 
       dpi = 300)
```

## Collinearity and Correlation Checks

```{r}
library(corrplot)
continuous_vars <- c("AGE", "LIMIT_BAL", 
                               paste0("BILL_AMT", 1:6), 
                               paste0("PAY_AMT", 1:6))

#Spearman(to be robust to skewness and detect non-linear correlation)
png(filename = "OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/spearman_correlation.png", 
    width = 1000, height = 1000, res = 120)

cor_matrix1 <- cor(data %>% select(all_of(continuous_vars)),
                  method = "spearman")



corrplot(cor_matrix1, 
         method = "color", 
         type = "upper", 
         tl.col = "black", 
         tl.srt = 45,
         addCoef.col = "black", # Add correlation coefficients
         number.cex = 0.6,      # Size of the coefficients
         title = "Correlation of Continuous Covariates (Spearman)",
         mar = c(0,0,1,0))
dev.off()

#Pearson

png(filename = "OUTPUT_IMAGES_EDA/pearson_correlation.png", 
    width = 1000, height = 1000, res = 120)

cor_matrix2 <- cor(data %>% select(all_of(continuous_vars)),
                  method = "pearson")
corrplot(cor_matrix2, 
         method = "color", 
         type = "upper", 
         tl.col = "black", 
         tl.srt = 45,
         addCoef.col = "black", # Add correlation coefficients
         number.cex = 0.6,      # Size of the coefficients
         title = "Correlation of Continuous Covariates (Pearson)",
         mar = c(0,0,1,0))

dev.off()
```
